source.title: SAGE: An Agentic Explainer Framework for Interpreting SAE Features in Language Models
source.authors: Jiao-Jiao Han; Wu-Jiang Xu; Ming-Yu Jin; Meng-Nan Du

page_placements.theme: Explanations fitted to top-activating examples (of SAE features, vision units and some neurons) predict activation over the rest of the range only partly

record.tranche_reason: Tests explanation prediction on held-out SAE-feature activations, a different measurement from the neuron audits in the claim. It does not audit neuron poles or report the proportion of neurons with one or two jobs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports predictive-accuracy results for SAE-feature explanations on held-out data; these bear on V6 and the automated scoring described in V7. The reported generative-accuracy comparisons concern generated text activating SAE features, not held-out prediction, so they are not included as rows. SAE features are not neuron poles, and the paper does not report the fraction of features that are monosemantic or polysemantic.
record.test_reason: The study scores explanations of SAE features, not neurons, using the simulation-based scoring from Bills et al. (an original source). It uses that score only to compare its own method (SAGE) with Neuronpedia. No result bears on any version as stated, since every version concerns neurons or neuron poles. The held-out SAE-feature scores are a related construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that SAGE yields SAE-feature explanations with higher generative and predictive accuracy than Neuronpedia, and that it captures multiple facets of polysemantic features.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates iterative, agent-generated explanations for SAE features using predictive correlation on held-out exemplars; the claim concerns audits of neuron poles and their job-count shares.
record.method_sensitivity: Predictive accuracy varies by model and layer; the ablation reports 0.648 at k = 5, 0.664 at k = 10, and 0.667 at k = 15, with different token costs.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-feature explanations written from top activating examples (Neuronpedia, GPT-5) reach held-out simulation correlations of 0.52–0.70. Iterative hypothesis testing (SAGE) raises this to 0.65–0.83. Qualitatively, example-based explanations overgeneralize, e.g. calling a can't-only feature a general n't detector.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For SAE features in LLMs (2B–20B), explanations from activating examples predict held-out activations only moderately (mean r ≈0.5–0.7). Active testing of explanations improves prediction modestly and narrows overbroad explanations.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The evaluation covers only 10 randomly sampled features at each of four selected layers per model, rather than all layers or features. It uses SAE features rather than neuron poles, and reports aggregate predictive correlations without a stated threshold for a good score or a neuron-level fraction.
record.rows_left_out: Generative-accuracy comparisons in Table 2 and the qualitative feature examples in Table 3 were left out because they do not measure held-out prediction or the neuron-level claims in V6–V7. No row is reported for the paper's cited findings from other work.

untested.parts: All: no neuron-pole audit of Qwen3-32B.
All: no neuron-level job shares in any model.
All: no InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
All: no neuron interpretability shares across architectures or tools.
Neuron explanations are not studied; only SAE features are.
Neuron explanations are not scored. No fraction of units with good scores is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked rows to V6 and V7 and labelled V6 supports. That linkage is not valid, because both versions concern neuron explanations and this study only explains SAE features; the record's own notes acknowledge this. The rows are mostly own-method vs baseline comparisons. Sample is 10 features per layer, with no uncertainty reported. The text's Neuronpedia baseline range of 0.52–0.70 matches Table 2.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole shares across models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, or trillion-parameter scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, and recursive generalization.
Neuron interpretability shares across architectures, regularization, tools, or InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons and reconstruction error.

The study tests SAE-feature explanations, not explanations of neurons; it does not specifically compare an explanation's fit to its source activating examples with its predictions on held-out activations.
The study scores SAE-feature explanations, not neuron explanations. It reports aggregate correlation metrics, not the proportion of neurons above a stated good-score threshold.

relation.reason: Uses simulation-style scoring (after Bills et al./Cunningham et al.) as an evaluation tool for its own method. Does not test the claim.

tranche.reason: Uses simulation-based predictive scoring on SAE features only to compare its own method (SAGE) with Neuronpedia. Gives no neuron-level result on any version.

source_check.notes: Units are SAE/transcoder features, not neurons, with 10 random features per layer. Table 2 layout is garbled but cells place cleanly by block order (GPT-OSS, Qwen, Gemma). Only r12 is wrong (0.66 should be 0.70). Qwen3-4b layer 11 shows no SAGE gain.

statements.correction: Text (Sec. 4.2, Table 2): Neuronpedia predictive accuracy 0.52-0.70, SAGE 0.65-0.83. Mean Pearson correlation of simulator-predicted vs true activations on held-out exemplars. Both methods use GPT-5 explanations from Neuronpedia top-k exemplars. One cell shows no gain: Qwen3-4b layer 11, 0.65 vs 0.65.
